title: MV Cropping images from different sides

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
I have a Window_Base, inside of which I've created a Sprite_Base with a bitmap.
This displays an image (woot).
I have figured out how to use setFrame() on the sprite to crop the image and make parts of it get cut off.
However, it always draws from the upper left of the frame, and therefore cuts off to the right and bottom.
How can I cut off the top or left of the image? The bitmap doesn't appear to have an anchor that specifies where it's attached to the sprite, and changing the sprite's anchor makes it go haywire out of the window containing it.
Am I approaching this entirely the wrong way?
Edit: I feel the answer is in Bitmap.blt, but I can't figure out how to make it produce a visual result. It seems to draw nothing. For example,
Code:
let bar = ImageManager.loadPicture("test");
    this.contents.blt(bar, 0, bar.height * percentage, bar.width, bar.height - bar.height * percentage, 0, 0);

Ah, I see how you got to this.
When an event starts, it looks through some specific commands and preloads any images they need. So drawFace doesn't need to account for an image not being loaded, but when making custom stuff you usually do.
The typical approach is similar to the one shared by
@Eliaquim
: created a listener for the image being loaded, and only do things with it when it's actually loaded.
So when the window is created, you'd do
JavaScript:
let barTemp = ImageManager.loadPicture("meter-bar");
barTemp.addLoadListener(() => {
    this.bar = barTemp;
});
And then only do blt when that
this.bar
exists.
For some examples,
here
is a window that simply displays a specific image, and
here
is a more complex one that displays a bunch of images that move on each frame.

Nice, I'm glad that worked. For an explanation as to why: Windows create their contents bitmap inside the constructor, and if you don't give them any arguments, it will be a 0x0 bitmap, unable to display anything. That bitmap is *not* resized when resizing the window (since it can't really be resized at all).
Click to expand...
